2004-Q9.q: What does 'contractile' mean for cardiac muscle?
wrong: It can stretch and spring back
2004-Q9.why: Contractile means able to contract: the muscle fibres shorten to squeeze blood out of the heart.

2004-Q9.q: Which heart chamber has the most muscle in its wall?
2004-Q9.why: The left ventricle pumps blood all round the body, so it needs the thickest, strongest wall.

2004-Q9.q: Describe how you dissected the heart to see the atria and ventricles. (3 points)
2004-Q9.right: Left side is firmer; cut it open with a scalpel on a board
wrong: Left side is softer; cut it open with a scalpel on a board
Right side is firmer; cut it open with a scalpel on a board
Left side is firmer; cut it open with forceps on a board
2004-Q9.why: Three of: tell left (firmer) from right, front side up, work on a board, use a scalpel, describe the cut, and a safety step.

2004-Q9.q: On your diagram, where should the bicuspid valve go?
2004-Q9.right: Between left atrium and left ventricle
wrong: Between right atrium and right ventricle
At the base of the aorta
At the base of the pulmonary artery
2004-Q9.why: The bicuspid valve is on the left side; the tricuspid is between the right atrium and right ventricle.

2004-Q9.q: How do you expose a semilunar valve?
2004-Q9.right: Cut open the aorta (or pulmonary artery)
2004-Q9.why: Semilunar valves sit at the base of the aorta and pulmonary artery, so you cut into those vessels.

2004-Q9.q: What does a semilunar valve do?
2004-Q9.right: Stops blood flowing back into the ventricle
wrong: Stops blood flowing back into the atrium
Lets blood pass from atrium to ventricle
2004-Q9.why: When the ventricle relaxes, the semilunar valve snaps shut so blood in the artery can't fall back in.

2004-Q9.q: Where does the coronary artery begin?
2004-Q9.right: At the base of the aorta
wrong: At the base of the pulmonary artery
In the wall of the right atrium
2004-Q9.why: The coronary arteries branch off the aorta just above the semilunar valve, bringing oxygen-rich blood.

2005-Q3.q: True or false: the SA node (pacemaker) is on the right side of the heart.
2005-Q3.why: The pacemaker sits in the wall of the right atrium, near where the vena cava enters.

2005-Q3.q: True or false: human red blood cells have no nucleus.
2005-Q3.why: Red blood cells lose their nucleus as they mature, which leaves more room for haemoglobin.

2006-Q5.q: On the diagram, which blood vessel is Y?
2006-Q5.why: Y links the intestine to the liver: that is the hepatic portal vein, carrying absorbed food.

2006-Q5.q: Which way does blood flow in Y, the hepatic portal vein?
2006-Q5.right: From the intestine into the liver
wrong: From the liver into the intestine
From the liver towards the heart
From the heart into the liver
2006-Q5.why: It carries food absorbed in the gut to the liver, so its arrow points towards the liver.

2006-Q13a.q: Where in the body are red blood cells made?
2006-Q13a.why: Red cells are made in the marrow of bones like the ribs, sternum and skull; liver and spleen break them down.

2006-Q13a.q: Give two ways red blood cells differ from cheek cells. (2 points)
2006-Q13a.right: They have no nucleus and contain haemoglobin
wrong: They have a nucleus and contain haemoglobin
They have no nucleus and have more mitochondria
They have no cell membrane and contain haemoglobin
2006-Q13a.why: Two of: red cells have no nucleus, no mitochondria, contain haemoglobin, carry oxygen, and are smaller biconcave discs.

2006-Q13b.q: Explain the terms plasma and glomerular filtrate. (2 points)
2006-Q13b.right: Plasma: liquid part of blood; filtrate: plasma minus its proteins
wrong: Plasma: blood cells and platelets; filtrate: plasma minus proteins
Plasma: liquid part of blood; filtrate: urine in the bladder
Plasma: liquid part of blood; filtrate: blood in the glomerulus
2006-Q13b.why: Two points: plasma is the liquid part of blood; glomerular filtrate is plasma (minus its proteins) that has passed into Bowman's capsule.

2006-Q13c.q: Which two parts make up the lymphatic system?
2006-Q13c.why: Lymph flows in lymph vessels, which pass through lymph nodes that filter it.

2006-Q13c.q: Which is a function of the lymphatic system? (one of 6 points)
2006-Q13c.right: Absorbs fats at the lacteals in villi
wrong: Absorbs glucose at the lacteals in villi
Carries oxygen to the body cells
2006-Q13c.why: Six points: three functions, each explained, e.g. returns tissue fluid to blood; absorbs fats at lacteals; nodes filter bacteria (defence).

2007-Q13a.q: Which vessel brings blood back to the heart from the lungs?
2007-Q13a.why: Veins carry blood to the heart: the pulmonary vein brings oxygen-rich blood from the lungs.

2007-Q13a.q: Name the main gas in the pulmonary vein's blood, and how it is carried. (2 points)
2007-Q13a.right: Oxygen, joined to haemoglobin in red blood cells
wrong: Carbon dioxide, joined to haemoglobin in red cells
Oxygen, as hydrogencarbonate in the plasma
Oxygen, carried inside white blood cells
2007-Q13a.why: Two points: the gas is oxygen, and it is carried joined to haemoglobin (which contains iron), as oxyhaemoglobin in red cells.

2009-Q13a.q: What are the two circuits of the circulatory system?
2009-Q13a.why: The pulmonary circuit goes to the lungs and back; the systemic circuit goes to the rest of the body.

2009-Q13a.q: Which circuit does the left ventricle pump blood into?
2009-Q13a.why: The left ventricle pumps blood into the aorta, which carries it round the body: the systemic circuit.

2009-Q13b.right: Force of blood pushing on artery walls
wrong: Number of heartbeats in a minute
Stretching of an artery at each beat
How fast blood flows in the veins
2009-Q13b.why: Blood pressure is the force blood exerts on vessel walls; the stretching of an artery is the pulse.

2009-Q13b.q: Which is an effect of a diet high in saturated fat?
wrong: Arteries widen and get more elastic
2009-Q13b.why: Saturated fat and cholesterol build up as plaque in artery walls, narrowing them and raising blood pressure.

2009-Q13b.q: Give two ways, besides colour, red blood cells differ from cheek cells. (2 points)
2009-Q13b.right: Full of haemoglobin and have no nucleus
wrong: Full of haemoglobin and have two nuclei
Full of mitochondria and have no nucleus
Full of haemoglobin and have a cell wall
2009-Q13b.why: Two of: red cells are full of haemoglobin, have no nucleus (or mitochondria), and are a biconcave disc shape.

2009-Q13b.q: What do the SA and AV nodes do?
2009-Q13b.right: Send impulses that make the heart contract
wrong: Supply the heart muscle with blood
Keep the two sides' blood apart
2009-Q13b.why: The nodes make and pass on electrical impulses: the SA node is the pacemaker that sets the heartbeat.

2009-Q13b.q: Where precisely are the SA node and the AV node? (2 points)
2009-Q13b.right: SA: right atrium wall; AV: septum near the tricuspid valve
wrong: SA: left atrium wall; AV: septum near the tricuspid valve
SA: right atrium wall; AV: at the base of the aorta
SA: right ventricle wall; AV: left atrium wall
2009-Q13b.why: Two points: the SA node is in the wall of the right atrium; the AV node is in the septum, near the tricuspid valve.

2010-Q7.q: Which body cavity holds the heart and lungs?
2010-Q7.why: The heart and lungs sit in the thorax, above the diaphragm; the abdomen is below it.

2010-Q7.q: How does heart muscle differ from other muscles?
wrong: It is attached to bones by tendons
2010-Q7.why: Cardiac muscle contracts all your life without fatigue, and it is involuntary.

2010-Q7.q: How can you tell the front (ventral) side of the heart? (one of 4 points)
2010-Q7.right: Coronary artery runs diagonally across it
wrong: Pulmonary veins enter on that side
No large vessels can be seen on it
2010-Q7.why: Four of: find the front, say how (coronary artery), name the scalpel, describe the first and second cuts, find a named structure, a safety step.

2010-Q7.q: How do you expose a semilunar valve?
2010-Q7.right: Cut open the pulmonary artery (or aorta)
2010-Q7.why: Semilunar valves sit where the aorta and pulmonary artery leave the ventricles, so you cut into those.

2010-Q7.q: In your drawing, which chamber sits above the tricuspid valve? (one of 4 points)
2010-Q7.why: Four points: a drawing of the dissection, labelled right atrium, tricuspid valve and right ventricle. The right atrium sits above the valve.

2010-Q15b.q: In your diagram, the hepatic portal vein links which organs?
2010-Q15b.why: The hepatic portal vein runs from the capillaries of the small intestine to the liver.

2010-Q15b.q: Which substance does the hepatic portal vein carry to the liver?
2010-Q15b.why: Glucose absorbed in the villi goes straight to the liver; starch must be digested first, and bile leaves the liver.

2010-Q15b.q: Which vessel brings oxygenated blood to the liver?
2010-Q15b.why: Arteries bring oxygen-rich blood to organs: the hepatic artery, a branch of the aorta, supplies the liver.

2011-Q8b.q: Why do heart and breathing rates rise during exercise? (2 points)
2011-Q8b.right: More O2 and energy needed; more CO2 to remove
wrong: More O2 and energy needed; less CO2 is made
Less O2 and energy needed; more CO2 to remove
Muscles make extra O2; more CO2 to remove
2011-Q8b.why: Two points: muscles need more oxygen and energy, and make more CO2 to get rid of.

2011-Q12b.q: Which vessel supplies blood to a kidney?
2011-Q12b.why: Arteries bring blood to organs: the renal artery, a branch of the aorta, supplies each kidney.

2012-Q7b.q: How did you expose the semilunar valves?
2012-Q7b.right: Cut open the aorta or pulmonary artery
2012-Q7b.why: The semilunar valves guard the openings of the aorta and pulmonary artery, so you cut into those.

2012-Q15b.q: Give two ways, other than colour, red cells differ from white cells. (2 points)
2012-Q15b.right: Red cells have no nucleus and contain haemoglobin
wrong: Red cells have a nucleus and contain haemoglobin
Red cells are larger and have no nucleus
Red cells have no nucleus and make antibodies
2012-Q15b.why: Two of: red cells have no nucleus, contain haemoglobin, are smaller, are biconcave discs, and are far more numerous than white cells.

2012-Q15b.q: Which is a group of white blood cells other than lymphocytes?
2012-Q15b.why: Phagocytes such as monocytes engulf germs; B cells are lymphocytes, and platelets aren't white cells.

2014-Q3.q: On the diagram, what is part C?
2014-Q3.why: C collects excess tissue fluid from around the body cells, so it is a lymph vessel.

2014-Q3.q: What type of blood vessel is A?
2014-Q3.why: A carries blood towards the capillaries, so it is an arteriole (a small artery); B drains them.

2014-Q3.q: How would a section through A differ from one through B?
wrong: A's wall is one cell thick
2014-Q3.why: A carries blood under higher pressure, so it has a thicker wall and narrower lumen than B.

2014-Q3.q: Which is a function of the lymphatic system? (one of 5 points)
2014-Q3.right: Returns excess tissue fluid to the blood
wrong: Carries oxygen to the body cells
2014-Q3.why: Five points: returns tissue fluid to the blood, makes or matures lymphocytes, filters bacteria, fights infection, and transports things like fats.

2014-Q3.q: How does lymph differ from blood?
2014-Q3.right: Lymph has no red blood cells
wrong: Lymph has no white blood cells
Lymph has less fat than blood
2014-Q3.why: Red cells are too big to leave capillaries, so lymph has none; it does carry white cells (lymphocytes).

2014-Q3.q: Which major vessel returns the blood in B to the heart?
2014-Q3.why: Blood from body tissues returns to the right atrium in the vena cava; pulmonary veins only drain the lungs.

2014-Q9b.right: Between right atrium and right ventricle
wrong: Between left atrium and left ventricle
At the base of the pulmonary artery
At the base of the aorta
2014-Q9b.why: Tricuspid is on the right, between right atrium and right ventricle; the bicuspid is on the left.

2014-Q9b.q: How do you cut to expose the tricuspid valve?
2014-Q9b.right: Cut open the right side with a scalpel
wrong: Cut open the left side with a scalpel
Cut open the aorta with a scalpel
Cut across the septum with a scalpel
2014-Q9b.why: The tricuspid valve is on the right side, so you open the right atrium and ventricle with a scalpel.

2014-Q9b.q: Where are the semilunar valves found?
2014-Q9b.right: At the base of the aorta and pulmonary artery
wrong: Between the atria and the ventricles
Where the venae cavae enter the atrium
2014-Q9b.why: Semilunar valves sit where the aorta and pulmonary artery leave the ventricles.

2014-Q9b.q: What did you measure first, before any exercise?
2014-Q9b.why: You need the resting rate first so you can compare the rates after exercise with it.

2014-Q9b.q: How did you measure pulse rate? (2 points)
2014-Q9b.right: Feel the pulse at the wrist; count beats for 1 minute
wrong: Feel the pulse in a wrist vein; count beats for 1 minute
Feel the wrist pulse; count for 1 minute, then divide by 60
Listen to the lungs; count the beats for 1 minute
2014-Q9b.why: Two of: feel the pulse (at the wrist or neck), count the beats for a set time such as 1 minute, then repeat and take the average.

2014-Q12c.q: Which capillary feature allows rapid uptake of CO2?
2014-Q12c.why: A wall one cell thick gives a very short distance for gases to diffuse across.

2014-Q12c.q: Why is there more CO2 in venous blood than arterial blood? (2 points)
2014-Q12c.right: Venous blood collects CO2 made by respiring body cells
wrong: Venous blood collects CO2 from the air in the lungs
Body cells use up the CO2 carried in arterial blood
CO2 from the air soaks into veins through the skin
2014-Q12c.why: Two points: venous blood has collected CO2 from respiring body cells, while arterial blood has had its CO2 cleared in the lungs.

2014-Q12c.q: Which vessel is an exception to this, and why?
2014-Q12c.right: Pulmonary vein: CO2 removed in the lungs
wrong: Renal vein: kidneys remove the CO2
Hepatic vein: liver removes the CO2
Vena cava: blood has been to the lungs
2014-Q12c.why: Pulmonary veins carry blood just cleared of CO2 in the lungs (the pulmonary artery is the reverse case).

2015-Q4.q: True or false: mitosis happens in mature human red blood cells.
2015-Q4.why: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus, so they cannot divide by mitosis.

2016-Q6.q: Why can't mature red blood cells divide?
2016-Q6.why: Cell division needs a nucleus with DNA to copy; mature red cells have lost theirs.

2016-Q8.right: Rhythmic stretching of an artery wall
wrong: Rhythmic stretching of a vein wall
Force of blood on the vessel walls
Sound of the heart valves closing
2016-Q8.why: Each heartbeat pushes a surge of blood into the arteries, stretching their walls: that is the pulse.

2016-Q8.q: Why is the wrist a good place to feel the pulse?
2016-Q8.right: An artery lies close to the skin there
wrong: A vein lies close to the skin there
Blood pressure is highest at the wrist
2016-Q8.why: At the wrist an artery runs near the surface, so you can feel it stretch with each beat.

2016-Q8.q: What was the control in this investigation?
wrong: The rate at the peak of exercise
The rate of a very fit athlete
2016-Q8.why: The resting rate is the baseline with no exercise, so it acts as the control.

2016-Q8.right: To compare the exercise results with
wrong: To make the results more reliable
To warm the person up first
2016-Q8.why: A control gives a baseline to compare with; repeating the test is what makes results reliable.

2016-Q8.q: On your graph, how should B's curve compare with A's?
2016-Q8.right: B's rate rises more than A's
wrong: A's rate rises more than B's
Both rise by exactly the same amount
2016-Q8.why: An unfit heart pumps less blood per beat, so B's rate has to rise more to supply her muscles.

2016-Q8.q: How would you measure recovery time? (3 points)
2016-Q8.right: Count pulse per minute right after exercise; time till it's resting
wrong: Count pulse per minute right before exercise; time till it peaks
Count pulse per minute right after exercise; time the exercise itself
Count red cells right after exercise; time till they're back to normal
2016-Q8.why: Three of: start immediately after exercise, count the pulse (or breaths) per minute, and time how long it takes to get back to the resting rate.

2016-Q15a.q: What should your drawings of a vein clearly show?
2016-Q15a.right: Thin wall, wide lumen and valves
wrong: Thick wall, narrow lumen, no valves
Wall one cell thick, no valves
Thick wall, wide lumen, no valves
2016-Q15a.why: Veins carry blood at low pressure, so they have thin walls, wide lumens and valves (seen in the L.S.).

2016-Q15a.q: Which vein has capillaries at both ends?
2016-Q15a.why: It starts in capillaries in the intestine and ends in capillaries in the liver.

2016-Q15a.q: How is blood moved along the veins?
2016-Q15a.right: Squeezed by muscles; valves stop backflow
wrong: Valves contract to pump it along
Strong pulses from the heart push it
Vein walls squeeze it by peristalsis
2016-Q15a.why: Skeletal muscles squeeze veins as they contract, and valves make sure blood only goes towards the heart.

2017-Q1.why: Haemoglobin has iron at its centre, which binds oxygen; magnesium is the metal in chlorophyll.

2018-Q11a.q: Name two substances, other than food and water, carried in blood. (2 points)
2018-Q11a.why: Two of: urea, hormones, antibodies, oxygen, CO2, plasma proteins, enzymes, clotting factors. Glucose and amino acids count as food.

2018-Q11a.q: Where does each enter the blood: urea and oxygen? (2 points)
2018-Q11a.right: Urea: at the liver; oxygen: at the lungs
wrong: Urea: at the kidneys; oxygen: at the lungs
Urea: at the liver; oxygen: at the heart
Urea: at the bladder; oxygen: at body cells
2018-Q11a.why: Two points: the liver makes urea from spare amino acids and puts it into the blood; oxygen enters the blood at the alveoli in the lungs.

2018-Q11b.q: In your heart drawing, which vessel leaves the right ventricle?
2018-Q11b.why: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs in the pulmonary artery; the aorta leaves the left ventricle.

2018-Q11b.q: What is the role of the AV node? (one of 4 points)
2018-Q11b.right: Passes the impulse on so ventricles contract
wrong: Starts each heartbeat in the atria
Stops blood flowing back into the atria
Separates the left and right ventricles
2018-Q11b.why: Four points: SA node is in the right atrium, sends impulses to make the atria contract; AV node is in the septum, passes them on to the ventricles.

2018-Q11b.q: What is measured when blood pressure is taken?
2018-Q11b.right: Force of blood against the artery wall
wrong: Amount of oxygen in the blood
Volume of blood pumped in each beat
2018-Q11b.why: Blood pressure is the force blood exerts on artery walls, read as systolic over diastolic.

2019-Q5.q: What word describes the shape of the two faces?
2019-Q5.why: Both faces dip inwards (concave), giving a big surface area for taking up oxygen.

2019-Q5.q: What lets red blood cells squeeze through narrow capillaries?
2019-Q5.right: They are flexible and can bend
2019-Q5.why: Red cells are flexible, so they can fold and bend to squeeze through capillaries narrower than themselves.

2019-Q5.q: Which molecule in red blood cells carries oxygen?
2019-Q5.why: Haemoglobin, with iron at its centre, picks up oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues.

2019-Q5.q: Why do red blood cells only live about 120 days?
2019-Q5.why: With no nucleus (or organelles) they can't make new proteins to repair themselves or divide.

2019-Q5.q: Where are red blood cells made, and where are they broken down?
2019-Q5.right: Made in marrow; broken down in liver
wrong: Made in spleen; broken down in kidney
Made in marrow; broken down in kidney
Made in kidney; broken down in liver
2019-Q5.why: Bone marrow makes red cells; old ones are broken down in the liver and spleen.

2019-Q5.q: Which transport fluid has no red blood cells?
2019-Q5.why: Lymph forms from fluid that leaks out of capillaries; red cells are too big to get out, so lymph has none.

2019-Q6.q: Which vessel does the lung capillary branch from?
2019-Q6.why: The pulmonary artery brings deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle and branches into lung capillaries.

2019-Q14b.q: Describe the sounds made during the cardiac cycle. (3 points)
2019-Q14b.right: Lub: bicuspid and tricuspid shut; dub: semilunar valves shut
wrong: Lub: semilunar valves shut; dub: bicuspid and tricuspid shut
Lub: bicuspid and tricuspid open; dub: semilunar valves open
Lub: the atria contract; dub: the ventricles contract
2019-Q14b.why: Three points: two sounds, 'lub' and 'dub', made by valves closing: 'lub' as the bicuspid and tricuspid shut, 'dub' as the semilunar valves shut.

2019-Q15b.q: Which vessel carries amino acids to the liver?
2019-Q15b.why: Amino acids enter blood capillaries in the villi, then the hepatic portal vein takes them to the liver.

2020-Q9.q: Why is blood in the right side kept apart from the left?
2020-Q9.right: Stops oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mixing
wrong: Stops blood flowing back into the atria
Lets blood pass from right side to left
Makes both sides pump at the same pressure
2020-Q9.why: Keeping them apart sends fully oxygenated blood to the body and lets each side pump at its own pressure.
Diastole is the relaxing phase when the chambers fill; systole is when the muscle contracts.

2020-Q9.q: How did you tell the left side from the right?
2020-Q9.right: Left side is thicker and firmer
wrong: Right side is thicker and firmer
Left side has the pulmonary artery
Left side has the vena cava
2020-Q9.why: The left ventricle's wall is much thicker, so that side feels firmer when you press it.

2020-Q9.q: Where did you see the coronary artery (groove)?
2020-Q9.why: The coronary artery runs diagonally across the front of the heart, on its outer surface.

2020-Q9.q: Where do you cut to find the bicuspid valve? (one of 4 points)
2020-Q9.right: Into the left side, atrium to ventricle
wrong: Into the right side, atrium to ventricle
Into the aorta, just above the heart
2020-Q9.why: Four of: a shallow cut, with a scalpel, on the left side, on a board (or a safety step), and the valve is between atrium and ventricle.

2020-Q9.q: Where is a semilunar valve, and how did you cut to find it? (2 points)
2020-Q9.right: At the base of the aorta; cut up into the aorta
wrong: Between left atrium and ventricle; cut into the aorta
At the base of the aorta; cut across the septum
Where the vena cava enters; cut into the vena cava
2020-Q9.why: Two points: a semilunar valve is at the base of the aorta (or pulmonary artery), and you cut up into that vessel to see it.

2021-Q14b.q: Which blood vessel carries digested nutrients from the gut?
2021-Q14b.why: Nutrients pass into blood capillaries in the villi, which join to form the hepatic portal vein.

2021-Q14b.q: Which organ do digested nutrients go to first?
2021-Q14b.why: The hepatic portal vein takes nutrients straight to the liver, which processes them before the heart.

2022-Q17d.q: What is the period when the heart muscle is not contracting?
2022-Q17d.why: Diastole is when heart muscle relaxes and the chambers fill; systole is the contracting phase.

2022-Q17d.q: In which diagram are the ventricles contracting, and how do you know? (2 points)
2022-Q17d.right: Z: the semilunar valves are open
wrong: Z: the semilunar valves are closed
Y: the semilunar valves are open
Z: the bicuspid and tricuspid are open
2022-Q17d.why: Two points: diagram Z, because its semilunar valves are open (and the AV valves shut) as blood is forced out into the arteries.
The SA node (pacemaker) is in the wall of the right atrium; the AV node is lower, in the septum.

2022-Q17d.q: Into which circuit does the right ventricle pump blood?
2022-Q17d.why: The right ventricle pumps blood through the pulmonary artery to the lungs: the pulmonary circuit.

2022-Q17d.q: What causes the two sounds of each heartbeat?
2022-Q17d.why: 'Lub' is the AV valves snapping shut and 'dub' is the semilunar valves snapping shut.

2022-Q17d.q: What does the coronary artery do?
2022-Q17d.right: Supplies the heart muscle with blood
wrong: Carries blood from the heart to lungs
Drains blood away from the heart muscle
Carries blood from the body to the heart
2022-Q17d.why: Heart muscle needs its own oxygen and food; coronary arteries bring it in, coronary veins drain it.

2022-Q17d.q: Which is an effect of smoking on the circulatory system?
2022-Q17d.why: Nicotine narrows blood vessels and speeds up the heart, raising blood pressure.

2023-Q6.q: Why is the septum needed in the heart?
2023-Q6.right: Stops oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood mixing
wrong: Stops blood flowing back into the atria
Lets blood pass from the right side to left
Supplies the heart wall with blood
2023-Q6.why: The septum is a wall keeping deoxygenated blood (right side) apart from oxygenated blood (left side).

2023-Q10b.q: Which instrument did you use to make the incisions?
2023-Q10b.why: A scalpel has a sharp blade for cutting; forceps hold tissue and a probe is for exploring.

2023-Q10b.q: How do the walls of the left and right ventricles differ?
wrong: Only the left wall contains muscle
2023-Q10b.why: The left ventricle pumps blood all round the body, so its muscular wall is much thicker than the right's.

2023-Q17c.q: Which vein carries blood lowest in metabolic wastes?
2023-Q17c.why: The kidneys filter urea and other wastes out, so blood leaving them in the renal vein has the least.

2024-Q6.q: Which pairing of systole and diastole is right?
2024-Q6.why: In systole heart muscle contracts and pumps blood out; in diastole it relaxes and the heart fills.

2025-Q16b.q: On the diagram, what is structure A?
2025-Q16b.why: A is the capillary carrying blood past the alveolus (B); its wall is one cell thick for fast diffusion.

2025-Q16d.q: Name two organs of the lymphatic system. (2 points)
2025-Q16d.why: Two of: lymph nodes, lymph vessels, spleen, thymus, tonsils, adenoids. The liver, pancreas and thyroid are not lymphatic organs.

2025-Q16d.q: Give two functions of the lymphatic system, other than maturing lymphocytes. (2 points)
2025-Q16d.right: Returns tissue fluid to the blood; fights infection
wrong: Returns tissue fluid to the blood; makes red blood cells
Carries oxygen to the body cells; fights infection
Removes urea from the blood; carries fats from the gut
2025-Q16d.why: Two of: returns excess tissue fluid to the blood, carries fats absorbed in the gut, and fights infection (lymph nodes filter out germs).

2025-Q17a.q: Which vessel carries blood highest in oxygen?
2025-Q17a.why: Blood in the pulmonary vein has just picked up oxygen in the lungs, so it is the richest in oxygen.

2025-Q17a.right: Keeps left and right sides' blood apart
wrong: Stops blood flowing back into the atria
Sets the pace of the heartbeat
Supplies blood to the heart muscle
2025-Q17a.why: The septum is a wall keeping oxygenated blood (left) apart from deoxygenated blood (right).

2025-Q17a.q: What is the period when heart muscle is contracting called?
2025-Q17a.why: Systole is the contracting phase; diastole is the relaxing phase when the chambers fill.

2025-Q17a.q: Give two structural differences between arteries and veins. (2 points)
2025-Q17a.right: Arteries: thick walls, no valves; veins: thin walls, valves
wrong: Arteries: thin walls, no valves; veins: thick walls, valves
Arteries: thick walls, valves; veins: thin walls, no valves
Arteries: wide lumen, no valves; veins: narrow lumen, valves
2025-Q17a.why: Two of: arteries have thicker walls, no valves and a narrower lumen; veins have thinner walls, valves and a wider lumen.

2026-Q7.q: Give the precise location and main function of the SA node. (2 points)
2026-Q7.right: Wall of the right atrium; it is the pacemaker
wrong: Wall of the left atrium; it is the pacemaker
Wall of the right atrium; it stops blood flowing back
Wall of the right ventricle; it is the pacemaker
2026-Q7.why: Two points: the SA node is in the wall of the right atrium, and it is the pacemaker, sending impulses that make the atria contract.

2026-Q16b.q: Why is a red blood cell a poor host for viruses?
2026-Q16b.right: No nucleus or organelles to copy the virus
wrong: It has a tough cell wall
It is too small for a virus to enter
2026-Q16b.why: Viruses need the host's nucleus and organelles (like ribosomes) to make copies; mature red cells have none.

2026-Q17a.q: What type of vessel are X and Y?
2026-Q17a.why: X, the arteriole, brings blood from an artery into the capillaries; Y, the venule, drains them to a vein.

wrong: Force of blood on the vessel walls
2026-Q17a.why: Each heartbeat sends a surge of blood that stretches artery walls; the force on the walls is blood pressure.

2026-Q17a.q: How does blood pressure change in the direction shown?
2026-Q17a.why: Pressure falls steadily as blood moves from the arteriole through the capillaries to the venule.

2026-Q17a.q: In your drawings, what should the artery show?
2026-Q17a.right: Thick muscular wall and small lumen
2026-Q17a.why: Arteries need thick, muscular, elastic walls to withstand high pressure; veins are thin with valves.

2026-Q17a.q: Which vessel in the capillary network soaks up excess tissue fluid?
2026-Q17a.why: Lymph vessels pick up the extra tissue fluid around the cells and return it to the blood as lymph.

2026-Q17a.q: Which is an effect of regular exercise?
2026-Q17a.why: Exercise strengthens the heart, so it pumps more per beat and the resting heart rate falls.

S1-Q3c.q: What is the main way CO2 is carried in the blood?
wrong: As gas bubbles in the plasma
S1-Q3c.why: Most CO2 reacts with water to form hydrogencarbonate (HCO3-) ions, which travel in the plasma.

S1-Q3c.q: What is the main way oxygen is carried in the blood?
S1-Q3c.right: As oxyhaemoglobin in red blood cells
S1-Q3c.why: Oxygen binds to haemoglobin in red cells to form oxyhaemoglobin; very little dissolves in plasma.

S1-Q3c.q: What goes in the table for arterial and venous pulmonary blood? (2 points)
S1-Q3c.right: Arterial: CO2 high, O2 low; venous: CO2 low, O2 high
wrong: Arterial: CO2 low, O2 high; venous: CO2 high, O2 low
Arterial: CO2 high, O2 high; venous: CO2 low, O2 low
Arterial: CO2 high, O2 low; venous: CO2 high, O2 low
S1-Q3c.why: Two points: pulmonary artery blood, going to the lungs, is high in CO2 and low in O2; pulmonary vein blood, coming back, is the reverse.

S1-Q5d.q: What are the two common blood grouping systems?
S1-Q5d.why: The ABO system (A, B, AB, O) and the Rhesus system (positive or negative) are the two main ones.

S1-Q5d.q: Why is it important to know a person's blood group?
wrong: To work out their heart rate
To choose which antibiotic to give
To find out if they are anaemic
S1-Q5d.why: Wrong-group blood makes the recipient's antibodies clump the donor red cells, which can be fatal.

S2-Q5a.q: On the diagram, which vessel is B?
S2-Q5a.why: B is the pulmonary artery, taking blood to the lungs; A is the aorta, taking blood to the body.

S2-Q5a.q: What happens to the labelled valve when the ventricles contract?
S2-Q5a.why: Blood forced out of the ventricle pushes the semilunar valve open; it shuts when the ventricle relaxes.

S2-Q5a.q: Where should X (the pacemaker) go on the diagram?
S2-Q5a.right: In the wall of the right atrium
wrong: In the wall of the left atrium
In the septum between the ventricles
At the base of the aorta
S2-Q5a.why: The pacemaker (SA node) is in the upper wall of the right atrium, near where the vena cava enters.

S2-Q5a.q: How does plasma CO2 change between A and B, and why? (2 points)
S2-Q5a.right: Higher in B: respiring cells added CO2; A lost CO2 in the lungs
wrong: Higher in A: respiring cells added CO2; B lost CO2 in the lungs
Higher in B: it took in CO2 from the air in the lungs
The same in both: CO2 stays in the red cells all the way
S2-Q5a.why: Two points: CO2 is higher in B (pulmonary artery), as respiring body cells added it; A (aorta) carries blood that lost CO2 in the lungs.

S2-Q5a.q: Which is a structural difference between an artery and a vein?
S2-Q5a.right: Veins have valves; arteries do not
wrong: Arteries have valves; veins do not
Veins have thicker walls than arteries
S2-Q5a.why: Blood in veins is at low pressure, so valves stop it flowing backwards; arteries have thick walls instead.

S2-Q5b.q: What are the two circuits called?
S2-Q5b.why: The pulmonary circuit takes blood to the lungs; the systemic circuit takes it round the rest of the body.

S2-Q5b.q: Describe the pathway of blood in the pulmonary circuit. (2 points)
S2-Q5b.right: Right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium
wrong: Right ventricle, pulmonary vein, lungs, pulmonary artery, left atrium
Left ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, right atrium
Right atrium, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left ventricle
S2-Q5b.why: Two points: name the circuit (pulmonary) and give its order: right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium.

S2-Q5b.q: What is the main effect of a fully blocked coronary artery?
S2-Q5b.right: Heart muscle gets no oxygen and dies
S2-Q5b.why: The blocked artery can't bring blood, so that part of the heart muscle can't respire and dies: a heart attack.

S2-Q5b.right: Force of blood on the vessel walls
wrong: Speed of blood through the veins
Amount of blood in the body
S2-Q5b.why: Blood pressure is the push of blood on artery walls; beats per minute is the heart (or pulse) rate.

S2-Q5c.q: On the graph, what causes each steep rise in pressure?
S2-Q5c.why: Each steep rise is the left ventricle contracting and forcing blood into the arteries: put X there.

S2-Q5c.q: From the graph, work out the heart rate, showing your working. (2 points)
S2-Q5c.right: One beat takes 0.5 s, so 60 / 0.5 = 120 bpm
wrong: One beat takes 0.5 s, so 60 x 0.5 = 30 bpm
One beat takes 1 s, so 60 / 1 = 60 bpm
One beat takes 0.25 s, so 60 / 0.25 = 240 bpm
S2-Q5c.why: Two points: one beat (peak to peak) takes 0.5 s, then divide 60 seconds by it: 60 / 0.5 = 120 beats per minute.

S2-Q5c.right: No: 120 bpm is too high for rest
wrong: Yes: 120 bpm is a normal resting rate
Yes: athletes always have fast hearts
No: athletes rest at over 150 bpm
S2-Q5c.why: A resting rate is about 60-80 bpm (lower in a fit athlete), so 120 bpm means the athlete is exercising.

S2-Q5d.q: Why do cardiac muscle cells have so many mitochondria? (2 points)
S2-Q5d.right: Heart never rests so needs lots of ATP, made by aerobic respiration
wrong: Heart never rests so needs lots of ATP, made by anaerobic respiration
Heart rests between beats so needs little ATP from respiration
Heart needs a big oxygen store, which mitochondria hold for it
S2-Q5d.why: Two points: heart muscle contracts nonstop and needs lots of energy (ATP); mitochondria release it by aerobic respiration, so it does not tire.
